# Data Construction

## Loading and Deduplication

```{r load-data}
source("datarade_helpers.R")

data_path <- if (file.exists("updated_datarade_data_scored_copy.jsonl")) {
  "updated_datarade_data_scored_copy.jsonl"
} else {
  file.path("data", "updated_datarade_data_scored_copy.jsonl")
}
lines <- readLines(data_path, warn = FALSE)
raw   <- lapply(lines, function(l) tryCatch(fromJSON(l), error = function(e) NULL))
raw   <- raw[!sapply(raw, is.null)]
urls  <- sapply(raw, function(r) r[["url"]] %||% NA_character_)
raw   <- raw[!duplicated(urls)]

df <- tibble(
  url = sapply(raw, function(r) r[["url"]] %||% NA_character_),
  provider_url = sapply(raw, function(r) {
    v <- r[["provider_url"]]
    if (is.null(v) || length(v) == 0) NA_character_ else as.character(v[1])
  }),
  # --- Clarity: continuous score + binary prediction ---
  C_score   = sapply(raw, function(r) as.numeric(r[["semantic_score"]] %||% NA_real_)),
  c_semantic = sapply(raw, function(r) as.integer(r[["semantic_pred"]] %||% NA_integer_)),
  # --- Temporal & Composability ---
  t_rank = sapply(raw, function(r)
    temporal_rank_full(r[["delivery"]], r[["details"]], r[["history"]])),
  k_hard_key_count = sapply(raw, function(r)
    hard_key_count_from_dd(r[["data_dictionary"]])),
  # --- Outcomes ---
  payment_modality      = sapply(raw, function(r)
    payment_modality_displayed(r[["pricing_plans"]])),
  price_displayed       = sapply(raw, function(r)
    price_displayed_from_metadata(r[["pricing_plans"]])),
  free_sample_available = sapply(raw, function(r)
    has_free_sample_offer(r[["details"]], r[["history"]],
                          r[["product-content__pricing-info"]], r[["delivery"]])),
  api_method            = sapply(raw, function(r) has_api_method(r[["delivery"]])),
  # --- Provider controls ---
  provider_rating = sapply(raw, function(r) {
    v <- r[["provider__rating-summary-score"]]
    if (is.null(v) || length(v) == 0 || !nzchar(as.character(v))) return(NA_real_)
    as.numeric(v[1])
  }),
  # --- Use-case tags ---
  use_cases = lapply(raw, function(r) {
    uc <- r[["use_cases"]]
    if (is.null(uc) || length(uc) == 0) return(character(0))
    as.character(unlist(uc))
  })
)

# Provider identifiers define the clustering level. Listings without one cannot
# contribute to provider-clustered inference and are excluded before variables
# are standardized or provider-level controls are constructed.
df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(provider_url), nzchar(provider_url))
```

## Variable Construction

Semantic clarity is measured by the **continuous classifier score** ($C_i^{\text{score}} \in [0.25,\,0.77]$)
produced by the LLM-based semantic classifier (GABRIEL).  This score reflects the
probability that a listing's content qualifies as semantically clear under the
ostension/transformation/contamination decision rules.  We also retain the binary
prediction ($C_i^{\text{pred}} \in \{0,1\}$, threshold $\approx 0.52$) for
comparison in the fsQCA.

Temporal intensity and composability use the same continuous operationalisations
as the main paper: cadence rank (0â€“9) and $\log(1 + \text{hard\_key\_count})$.

```{r construct-variables}
df <- df %>% mutate(
  # Continuous conditions
  T_rank   = pmax(t_rank, 0L),                                       # 0â€“9
  K_log    = log1p(k_hard_key_count),                                 # 0â€“~5
  # Outcome count
  across(c(payment_modality, price_displayed, free_sample_available, api_method),
         ~replace_na(., 0L)),
  liquidity_count = payment_modality + price_displayed +
    free_sample_available + api_method,                               # 0â€“4
  # Legacy binary
  J_i = as.integer(c_semantic == 1 & T_rank >= 5 & k_hard_key_count >= 1)
)

# IDL composite (standardised)
df <- df %>% mutate(
  IDL_raw = scale(C_score)[,1] + scale(T_rank)[,1] + scale(K_log)[,1],
  IDL_std = as.numeric(scale(IDL_raw))
)

# Provider n (listing count)
prov_n <- df %>% count(provider_url, name = "provider_n")
df <- left_join(df, prov_n, by = "provider_url") %>%
  mutate(
    provider_n = replace_na(provider_n, 1L),
    rating_missing  = as.integer(is.na(provider_rating)),
    provider_rating = replace_na(provider_rating, 0)
  )

# Parsimonious multilabel use-case controls: retain tags present in at least 2%
# of the provider-identified sample and remove exact duplicate tag profiles.
df_base <- df
uc_design <- make_prevalent_use_case_controls(df, min_share = 0.02)
df <- uc_design$data
uc_cols <- uc_design$columns
N_uc_raw <- uc_design$retained_tags
N_uc_duplicate <- length(uc_design$duplicate_profiles_removed)

# IDL quintile
df$IDL_Q <- cut(df$IDL_std,
                breaks = quantile(df$IDL_std, probs = 0:5/5, na.rm = TRUE),
                include.lowest = TRUE, labels = paste0("Q", 1:5))

N_obs <- nrow(df)
N_prov <- n_distinct(df$provider_url)
N_uc   <- length(uc_cols)
```

The estimation sample contains **`r format(N_obs, big.mark=",")`** unique product
listings from **`r N_prov`** identified providers. The parsimonious use-case design
retains tags appearing in at least **`r uc_design$min_n` listings** (2% of the
sample), yielding **`r N_uc`** distinct indicator profiles after removing
**`r N_uc_duplicate`** exact duplicate profile.

The use-case field is treated as multilabel rather than mutually exclusive.
Tag strings are trimmed, converted to lower case, and empty values are removed;
each retained tag then becomes a binary listing-level indicator. All retained
indicators enter jointly as nuisance controls for intended application. Tags
below the prevalence threshold are not pooled into an `other` category. Exact
duplicate indicator profiles are removed deterministically, without consulting
the outcome or the data-liquidity index, to avoid collinearity between tags that
are always assigned together.

| Symbol | Measure | Range | Construction |
|--------|---------|------:|--------------|
| $C_i$ | Semantic clarity | [0.25, 0.77] | LLM classifier probability (`semantic_score`) |
| $T_i$ | Temporal intensity | 0â€“9 | Maximum cadence rank (historical=0 â€¦ real-time=9) |
| $K_i$ | Composability | 0â€“~5 | $\log(1 + \text{hard\_key\_count})$ |
| $\text{IDL}_i$ | Composite index | continuous | Standardised sum of $z(C_i) + z(T_i) + z(K_i)$ |
| $Y_i$ | Realized liquidity | 0â€“4 | Sum of four transactional-readiness signals |

# Descriptive Statistics

## Summary Statistics

```{r tbl-summary}
summ <- df %>%
  summarise(
    across(c(C_score, T_rank, K_log, IDL_std, liquidity_count,
             payment_modality, price_displayed, free_sample_available, api_method,
             provider_n, provider_rating),
           list(
             Mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
             SD   = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE),
             Min  = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
             Med  = ~median(., na.rm = TRUE),
             Max  = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
           ), .names = "{.col}__{.fn}")
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"),
               names_sep = "__")

var_labels <- c(
  C_score   = "Semantic Clarity (C)",
  T_rank    = "Temporal Intensity (T)",
  K_log     = "Composability (K)",
  IDL_std   = "IDL Index (std.)",
  liquidity_count   = "Liquidity Count (Y)",
  payment_modality  = "Payment Modality",
  price_displayed   = "Price Displayed",
  free_sample_available = "Free Sample",
  api_method        = "API Delivery",
  provider_n        = "Provider Listing Count",
  provider_rating   = "Provider Rating"
)
summ$Variable <- var_labels[summ$Variable]

kbl(summ, digits = 3, col.names = c("Variable", "Mean", "SD", "Min", "Median", "Max"),
    caption = paste0("Table 1: Summary Statistics (N = ", format(N_obs, big.mark=","), ")")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  pack_rows("IDL Conditions", 1, 4) %>%
  pack_rows("Outcomes", 5, 9) %>%
  pack_rows("Controls", 10, 11)
```

## Correlation Matrix

```{r tbl-corr}
cor_vars <- df %>% select(C_score, T_rank, K_log, IDL_std, liquidity_count)
cor_mat  <- cor(cor_vars, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Pretty labels
rownames(cor_mat) <- colnames(cor_mat) <- c("C", "T", "K", "IDL", "Y")

kbl(round(cor_mat, 3),
    caption = "Table 2: Pairwise Correlations") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## IDL Quintile Gradient

```{r fig-quintile, fig.cap="Figure 1: Mean Realized Liquidity by IDL Quintile"}
q_means <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(IDL_Q)) %>%
  group_by(IDL_Q) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    mean_model <- lm(liquidity_count ~ 1, data = .x)
    mean_ct <- cluster_coeftable(mean_model, .x$provider_url)
    tibble(
      mean_liq = coef(mean_model)[1],
      se = mean_ct["(Intercept)", "Std. Error"],
      n = nrow(.x)
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(q_means, aes(x = IDL_Q, y = mean_liq)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8", width = 0.65) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_liq - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean_liq + 1.96 * se),
                width = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_liq)), vjust = -1.5, size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .15))) +
  labs(x = "IDL Quintile", y = "Mean Liquidity Count (0â€“4)") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

# Main Specification: Poisson Regression {.tabset}

## Model

The outcome $Y_i \in \{0,1,2,3,4\}$ counts how many transactional-readiness
signals a listing activates.  Because the outcome is a bounded count with
moderate overdispersion, we estimate a **Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood**
model with standard errors clustered by provider:

$$
E[Y_i \mid \mathbf{X}_i] = \exp\!\Big(\alpha + \beta\,\text{IDL}_i^{\text{std}}
  + \gamma_1\,\text{provider\_n}_i + \gamma_2\,\text{provider\_rating}_i
  + \gamma_3\,\mathbf{1}_{\text{rating missing}}
  + \sum_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \delta_u\, U_{iu}\Big)
$$

The coefficient $\beta$ is interpreted as an **incidence-rate ratio (IRR)**:
$e^\beta$ gives the multiplicative change in expected liquidity count for a
one-standard-deviation increase in the IDL index.

```{r main-poisson}
fml_main <- as.formula(
  paste0("liquidity_count ~ IDL_std + provider_n + provider_rating + rating_missing + ",
         paste(uc_cols, collapse = " + "))
)

m_pois <- glm(fml_main, data = df, family = poisson(link = "log"))

# Extract key stats
coefs <- cluster_coeftable(m_pois, df$provider_url)
b     <- coefs["IDL_std", "Estimate"]
se_b  <- coefs["IDL_std", "Std. Error"]
t_b   <- coefs["IDL_std", "t value"]
p_b   <- coefs["IDL_std", "Pr(>|t|)"]
irr   <- exp(b)
main_ci <- cluster_confint(coefs)
irr_lo <- exp(main_ci["IDL_std", "lower"])
irr_hi <- exp(main_ci["IDL_std", "upper"])
n_obs <- nobs(m_pois)
ll    <- logLik(m_pois)
pr2   <- 1 - as.numeric(ll) / as.numeric(logLik(glm(liquidity_count ~ 1, data = df,
                                                    family = poisson(link = "log"))))
```

## Results

```{r tbl-main-result}
main_tbl <- tibble(
  ` ` = c("IDL (std.)", "", "Provider listing count", "Provider rating",
          "Use-case controls", "Observations", "Pseudo RÂ²"),
  `Coefficient` = c(
    sprintf("%.4f", b), sprintf("(%.4f)", se_b),
    sprintf("%.4f", coefs["provider_n", "Estimate"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", coefs["provider_rating", "Estimate"]),
    paste0(N_uc, " included"),
    format(n_obs, big.mark = ","),
    sprintf("%.4f", pr2)
  ),
  `IRR` = c(
    sprintf("%.3f", irr), "",
    sprintf("%.3f", exp(coefs["provider_n", "Estimate"])),
    sprintf("%.3f", exp(coefs["provider_rating", "Estimate"])),
    "", "", ""
  ),
  `95% CI` = c(
    sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", irr_lo, irr_hi), "",
    "", "", "", "", ""
  ),
  `p` = c(
    ifelse(p_b < 0.001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", p_b)), "",
    ifelse(coefs["provider_n", "Pr(>|t|)"] < 0.001, "< .001",
           sprintf("%.3f", coefs["provider_n", "Pr(>|t|)"])),
    ifelse(coefs["provider_rating", "Pr(>|t|)"] < 0.001, "< .001",
           sprintf("%.3f", coefs["provider_rating", "Pr(>|t|)"])),
    "", "", ""
  )
)

kbl(main_tbl,
    caption = "Table 3: Main Specification: Poisson Regression of Liquidity Count on IDL",
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  footnote(general = paste0("Poisson PML with provider-clustered SEs (",
                            N_prov, " clusters). ", N_uc,
                            " prevalent use-case indicators retained (â‰¥2% of listings)."))
```

**Interpretation.** A one-standard-deviation increase in the IDL index
raises the expected number of transactional-readiness signals by a factor
of **`r sprintf("%.3f", irr)`** (IRR, 95% CI [`r sprintf("%.3f", irr_lo)`,
`r sprintf("%.3f", irr_hi)`], *p* < .001).

## Use-Case Control Parsimony

The primary 2% prevalence rule is fixed independently of the outcome. To assess
whether the result depends on that cutoff, we re-estimate the provider-clustered
Poisson model at nearby thresholds. This retains the marketplace's multilabel
use-case structure while avoiding hundreds of sparse nuisance parameters.

```{r use-case-threshold-sensitivity}
uc_threshold_results <- lapply(c(0.01, 0.015, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05), function(threshold) {
  design <- make_prevalent_use_case_controls(df_base, min_share = threshold)
  d <- design$data
  f <- as.formula(
    paste0("liquidity_count ~ IDL_std + provider_n + provider_rating + rating_missing + ",
           paste(design$columns, collapse = " + "))
  )
  model <- glm(f, data = d, family = poisson(link = "log"))
  ct <- cluster_coeftable(model, d$provider_url)
  ci <- cluster_confint(ct)
  tibble(
    `Minimum prevalence` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * threshold),
    `Minimum listings` = design$min_n,
    `Use-case controls` = length(design$columns),
    IRR = exp(ct["IDL_std", "Estimate"]),
    `95% CI lower` = exp(ci["IDL_std", "lower"]),
    `95% CI upper` = exp(ci["IDL_std", "upper"]),
